stories.title: Sydney airport near-miss involved controllers flagged as high-fatigue risk, records show
stories.summary: Sept 4 - Several air traffic controllers on duty when two Qantas aircraft nearly collided at Sydney airport in July had been flagged as facing a high risk of fatigue, according to internal records and a call recording obtained by Reuters, a staffing situation one shift manager described as "a bit insane". The July 27 incident, in which a landing Qantas turboprop narrowly avoided a Qantas Boeing 737 that had been cleared to cross the runway, was the first of six near-misses at Sydney Airport in about a month, drawing further scrutiny of air traffic control staffing amid global shortages. Of the 10 controllers on duty at the time, five were rated "H" for high fatigue risk under Australia's fatigue-management system, according to an internal log reviewed by Reuters. One was rated "M" for medium risk and one was "L" for low risk. The other three were not ranked as at risk of fatigue. "We've got like five high fatigues on this morning. It's a bit insane," a controller shift manager told an air traffic management director in an internal call after the near-miss. "Thankfully, they didn't hit, but it was pretty close and everyone up here is pretty rattled by it," he said in a recording reviewed by Reuters. Two of the three controllers directly involved in the incident were “high fatigued” and the third was “medium fatigued,” the shift manager said. The fatigue-risk ratings and the internal call, neither of which has previously been reported, occurred as aviation authorities worldwide grapple with concerns about overstretched air traffic control workforces and the risk of accidents. Airservices Australia, the government agency that employs the country's air traffic controllers, declined to comment, citing the ongoing investigation into the incident. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating all six near-misses to determine whether they share common safety issues or contributing factors.

stories.title: The dedicated band of district correspondents
stories.summary: For five decades, the district correspondents chronicled the changing face of united Andhra Pradesh, taking the newspaper beyond capitals and corridors of power into villages, conflict zones and remote hinterlands. From painstaking trunk-call filings to laptops and digital reporting, they brought grassroots voices, rural concerns, political shifts, social movements and crises to readers, becoming the quiet pillars of the newspaper’s credibility and legacy. They laid the foundation for what became one of the strongest district reporting networks among English-language newspapers in the State

stories.summary: The latest US visa restrictions on citizens of African countries are facing increasing criticism that they are not only punitive but also likely to backfire by driving those nations closer to China. Since August 1, visa services have been suspended in 25 African cities, forcing applicants to travel to other approved locations, sometimes in another country. stories.headline: China stands to gain from US visa restrictions targeting African countries

opening: The latest US visa restrictions on citizens of African countries are facing increasing criticism that they are not only punitive but also likely to backfire by driving those nations closer to China.
Since August 1, visa services have been suspended in 25 African cities, forcing applicants to travel to other approved locations, sometimes in another country.
